== main.c#L1-L43
     1  /* The harness for the compiled checker: the trusted C side of the end-to-end theorem.
     2  
     3     build:  make   (cc -std=gnu23 -O2 -pthread -o checker main.c checker.s; Makefile)
     4     usage:  checker [--jobs=N] FILE
     5  
     6     The default path is the one the final theorem covers (`checkerFile_accepts`,
     7     ConAgua/Final/EndToEnd.lean; the call is as `AbiCall` in ConAgua/Final/Abi.lean states it).
     8     It maps FILE (the input) read-only, or reads it whole into a buffer if it is not a regular
     9     file (`read_input`); the theorem is about the bytes the buffer holds, so a file that another
    10     process changes during the run is outside it. It maps one zero region of ca_region_size
    11     bytes and calls, once,
    12  
    13       ca_start(in, in_len, pins, pins_len, region, region_len)
    14  
    15     with the pin data `pins` built into the binary (below). `ca_start` is the sequential driver:
    16     entry 1 (the stages and phase A), then entry 2 over every pending group, on the same region;
    17     the entry stubs lay out everything else inside the region. The verdict is one line on stdout,
    18     and the exit status follows the Lean kernel arena's convention (0 accepted, 1 rejected,
    19     2 declined, 3 error):
    20       accept         0  rdx = 0 and rax = ACCEPT (0x414343455054): the only accept
    21       rejected: M    1  rdx = 2, class 1: the checker aborted where the twin fails as invalid
    22       declined: M    2  rdx = 2, class 2: the checker aborted where the twin fails as not
    23                         implemented
    24       error: M       3  rdx = 2, class 0: any other abort (a capacity of the checker, a check the
    25                         twin does not make, an out-of-bounds access); claims nothing
    26       exhausted      3  rdx = 1: fuel, stack or region ran out
    27       ok R           3  rdx = 0 and any other rax R, in decimal (1: the frontend rejected a malformed
    28                         line, which con-leche reports as an error too)
    29     On an abort, rax is its code: the class in bits 0-1, the reason in bits 2 and up, whose
    30     message M is reasons[reason] (reasons.h, generated from the twin's own messages; reason 0
    31     prints no message). The classes are proved (`checkerFile_accepts`): rdx = 2 with class 1 or 2
    32     means the twin's pipeline fails on the input with `invalid` resp. `notImplemented`; the
    33     messages are not part of the theorem.
    34     A failure of the harness itself (usage, a file that cannot be read, no memory) prints a
    35     message on stderr and exits with status 3 and no verdict line. A crash (e.g. a page of the
    36     region the kernel cannot supply) prints nothing and ends with a signal. None is an accept.
    37  
    38     With --jobs=N for N > 1, the threaded mode, `run_jobs` below: its accept is covered by
    39     `checkerFile_threads_accept` (ConAgua/Final/EndToEnd.lean), under the hypotheses
    40     `ThreadsRun` (ConAgua/Final/ThreadsFinal.lean) states about this harness's threads. A failing
    41     threaded run prints the verdict of the failing group with the smallest index, which is what the
    42     sequential run prints; a reject or decline is covered by `checkerFile_threads_verdict`, under
    43     the hypotheses `ThreadsFail` (ConAgua/Final/ThreadsVerdict.lean) states about the failing call. */

== main.c#L83-L95
    83  /* Prints the verdict line and returns the exit status (the table above). */
    84  static int print_verdict(ca_res r) {
    85    if (accepted(r)) { printf("accept\n"); return 0; }
    86    if (r.rdx == 0) { printf("ok %llu\n", (unsigned long long)r.rax); return 3; }
    87    if (r.rdx == 1) { printf("exhausted\n"); return 3; }
    88    uint64_t cls = r.rax & 3, why = r.rax >> 2;
    89    const char *msg = why < sizeof reasons / sizeof *reasons ? reasons[why] : "unknown reason";
    90    const char *sep = why ? ": " : "";
    91    if (cls == 1) { printf("rejected%s%s\n", sep, msg); return 1; }
    92    if (cls == 2) { printf("declined%s%s\n", sep, msg); return 2; }
    93    printf("error%s%s\n", sep, msg);
    94    return 3;
    95  }

== ConAgua/Compiler/Main.lean#L28-L31
    28  def OutcomeRel (G : Layout) : Except Err (List Word × Mem) → MachineData → Prop
    29    | .ok (rs, m'), s => s.regs.rdx = 0 ∧ ResOut G G.tab.nres rs s ∧ MemRel G m' s.dmem
    30    | .error .outOfFuel, _ => False
    31    | .error e, s => s.regs.rdx = 2 ∧ s.regs.rax = e.code

== docs/deviations.md#L49
    49  | D16 | the abort sites (`fail R`, `ConAgua/Arena/Reasons.lean`) | each `fail` has its kind (`invalid`, `notImplemented`, `internal`, `native`) and message | an abort carries a class (reject, decline, other) and a reason: the twin's reject/decline sites are labelled with the twin's message; class 0 (exit 3) at every capacity or defensive check (an unresolved constant decides its kind as the twin does, `unresolved_consts_error`: a string literal before `String` or a use of `sorryAx` declines, anything else rejects; its two walks, `has_str_lit_go` and `ue_mentions_go`, drop the twin's memo so the error path writes nothing: the same answer, but exponential time on a heavily shared term, error path only) | completeness of the verdict only: L says `error` where the twin rejects or declines | – | by design: the classes are proved (a reject or decline is the twin's, the final theorems); the messages are not part of the theorem |

== ConAgua/Final/Statement.lean#L88-L90
    88  /-- The verdict word `check` returns first for accept. Not `0`, `1` or `2`, so that a status word
    89  or an unset register is never read as accept. -/

== ConAgua/Final/EndToEnd.lean#L80-L87
    80  theorem checkerFile_accepts [Host]
    81      (k0 : Nat) (hcode : Code checkerFile k0)
    82      (b pb : ByteArray) (h64 : System.Platform.numBits = 64)
    83      (dm : MachineData) (ra : Word) (hc : AbiCall b pb dm ra) :
    84      Ev (fun st => st.pc = Int64.ofBitVec ra.toBitVec ∧
    85          (st.data.regs.rdx = 0 → st.data.regs.rax = ACCEPT → TwinAccepts [b]) ∧
    86          (st.data.regs.rdx = 2 → st.data.regs.rax &&& 3 ≠ 0 →
    87            TwinVerdict [b] (st.data.regs.rax &&& 3)))

    25  /-- Every run from `d` at `pc` reaches `Q`. -/
    26  abbrev Ev (Q : MachineState → Prop) (d : MachineData) (pc : Int64) : Prop :=

== ConAgua/Final/Twin.lean#L57-L67
    57  /-- **The twin accepts `chunks`**: the stages con-ron's binary runs, from the twin's start state
    58  `AState.init EStore.empty`, at some pin list, the fold on one worker. -/
    59  def TwinAccepts (chunks : List ByteArray) : Prop :=
    60    ∃ (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (sA sB sC sD sE sF : AState) (pre : PreludeIx) (r : ParseResultD)
    61      (ds : Array IDeclaration) (ipins : List INatOpPinSet) (fe : IFEnv),
    62      internReservedPins (AState.init EStore.empty) = .ok ((), sA) ∧
    63      builtinPreludeE sA = .ok (.ok pre, sB) ∧
    64      parseChunks chunks sB = .ok (.ok r, sC) ∧
    65      preparePrelude pre r.decls sC = .ok (ds, sD) ∧
    66      internAllPins pins sD = .ok (ipins, sE) ∧
    67      SeqAccepts .verified ipins ds sE fe sF

== ConAgua/Final/Twin.lean#L39-L45
    39  /-- **The x64 checker's fold**: phase A accepted with environment `fe` and pending records `pend`,
    40  ending in `s'`; phase B, every pending record in order on one worker made from `s'`, accepted. -/
    41  def SeqAccepts (mode : CheckMode) (pins : List INatOpPinSet) (ds : Array IDeclaration)
    42      (s : AState) (fe : IFEnv) (s' : AState) : Prop :=
    43    ∃ (n : Nat) (pend : Array PendingCheck) (s'' : AState),
    44      installFold mode pins (0, mkIFEnv IEnv.empty, #[]) ds.toList s = .ok (.ok (n, fe, pend), s') ∧
    45      checkPendingList mode fe pend.toList s'.worker = .ok (.ok (), s'')

== ConAgua/Final/TwinVerdict.lean#L58-L59
    58  def TwinVerdict (chunks : List ByteArray) (c : L.Word) : Prop :=
    59    ∃ pins, TwinFailsV (twinRun pins chunks) (AState.init EStore.empty) c

== ConAgua/Final/TwinVerdict.lean#L46-L54
    46  def twinRun (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (chunks : List ByteArray) :
    47      AM (Except (ConRon.Arena.CheckError × Nat) Unit) :=
    48    internReservedPins >>= fun _ =>
    49    thenV builtinPreludeE fun pre =>
    50    thenV (parseChunks chunks) fun r =>
    51    preparePrelude pre r.decls >>= fun ds =>
    52    internAllPins pins >>= fun ipins =>
    53    thenV (installFold .verified ipins (0, mkIFEnv IEnv.empty, #[]) ds.toList) fun q =>
    54    fun s => checkPendingList .verified q.2.1 q.2.2.toList s.worker

== ConAgua/Final/Twin.lean#L119-L135
   119  /-- **What the twin's accept means, in con-leche's terms**: con-leche's parser reads the chunks, and
   120  con-leche's pure fold accepts the parsed records prepared with some prelude, at the twin's pin
   121  list. `stages_frame`, then Theorem 1 (`Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge`, with its two tier specs
   122  discharged by `CoreSpec.of_core` and `indSpec_of_bridge`). -/
   123  theorem twinAccepts_pure {chunks : List ByteArray} (h : TwinAccepts chunks) :
   124      ∃ (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (preC : ConLeche.Frontend.PreludeIx)
   125        (rc : ConLeche.Frontend.ParseResultD) (F : Nat) (env : Env),
   126        ConLeche.Frontend.parseChunks chunks = .ok rc ∧
   127        checkDeclsPure .verified (fueledOps .verified F) pins
   128          (ConLeche.Frontend.preparePrelude preC rc.decls).toList = .ok env := by
   129    obtain ⟨pins, sA, sB, sC, sD, sE, sF, pre, r, ds, ipins, fe, hA, hB, hC, hD, hE, hF⟩ := h
   130    have hk : CoreSpec .verified ConRon.Arena.checkFuel := CoreSpec.of_core rfl
   131    have hind : IndSpec .verified := ConRon.Bridge.Inductives.indSpec_of_bridge rfl hk
   132    obtain ⟨-, hfold, hipins, hpps, hpd, preC, rc, hrc, hden⟩ := stages_frame hA hB hC hD hE
   133    obtain ⟨env, F, -, hpure⟩ :=
   134      ConRon.Bridge.Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge rfl hk hind hpps hfold hipins hpd hden (pooledAccepts_of_seq hF)
   135    exact ⟨pins, preC, rc, F, env, hrc, hpure⟩

== ConAgua/Final/Statement.lean#L119-L126
   119  /-- **The caller's registers are intact on return**, relative to the registers `r0` at the call:
   120  `rsp` is past the return address and the other callee-saved registers of System V, `rbp`,
   121  `r14`, `r15`, `rbx`, `r12`, `r13`, hold their values from the call. The trampoline `ca_enter`
   122  saves and restores them (`rbp`, `r14` on the machine stack, the others past the table), so this
   123  holds whatever registers the compiled code uses. Together with the verdict in `rdx`/`rax` this is
   124  all the harness relies on after the call. -/
   125  def RegsRestored (r0 r : Reg64s) : Prop :=
   126    r.rsp.toNat = r0.rsp.toNat + 8 ∧ r.rbp = r0.rbp ∧ r.r14 = r0.r14 ∧ r.r15 = r0.r15 ∧

== ConAgua/Final/Abi.lean#L22-L48
    22  /-- **How the harness calls `ca_start`**: System V arguments `rdi, rsi` = the input buffer and its
    23  length, `rdx, rcx` = the pin-data buffer and its length, `r8, r9` = the region and its length;
    24  the buffers hold `b` and `pb`; the region is zero, in the address space, and apart from both
    25  buffers; the buffers are apart from each other; the return address is on the machine stack, whose
    26  32 bytes around `rsp` are mapped and apart from the region and the buffers. -/
    27  structure AbiCall (b pb : ByteArray) (dm : MachineData) (ra : Word) : Prop where
    28    hin : ∀ i (h : i < b.size), dm.dmem.get? (A (dm.regs.rdi.toNat + i)) = some b[i]
    29    hn : dm.regs.rsi.toNat = b.size
    30    hpins : ∀ i (h : i < pb.size), dm.dmem.get? (A (dm.regs.rdx.toNat + i)) = some pb[i]
    31    hnp : dm.regs.rcx.toNat = pb.size
    32    hzero : ∀ x, dm.regs.r8.toNat ≤ x → x < dm.regs.r8.toNat + dm.regs.r9.toNat → dm.dmem.get? (A x) = some 0
    33    hfits : dm.regs.r8.toNat + dm.regs.r9.toNat < 2 ^ 64
    34    hinEnd : dm.regs.rdi.toNat + b.size < 2 ^ 64
    35    hpinsEnd : dm.regs.rdx.toNat + pb.size < 2 ^ 64
    36    hinDisj : ∀ x, dm.regs.rdi.toNat ≤ x → x < dm.regs.rdi.toNat + b.size →
    37      x < dm.regs.r8.toNat ∨ dm.regs.r8.toNat + dm.regs.r9.toNat ≤ x
    38    hpinsDisj : ∀ x, dm.regs.rdx.toNat ≤ x → x < dm.regs.rdx.toNat + pb.size →
    39      x < dm.regs.r8.toNat ∨ dm.regs.r8.toNat + dm.regs.r9.toNat ≤ x
    40    hbufDisj : ∀ x, dm.regs.rdi.toNat ≤ x → x < dm.regs.rdi.toNat + b.size →
    41      ¬ (dm.regs.rdx.toNat ≤ x ∧ x < dm.regs.rdx.toNat + pb.size)
    42    hra : rdW dm.dmem (A dm.regs.rsp.toNat) = some ra
    43    hcs : ∀ x, dm.regs.rsp.toNat - 24 ≤ x → x < dm.regs.rsp.toNat + 8 →
    44      (dm.dmem.get? (A x)).isSome ∧ (x < dm.regs.r8.toNat ∨ dm.regs.r8.toNat + dm.regs.r9.toNat ≤ x) ∧
    45      ¬ (dm.regs.rdi.toNat ≤ x ∧ x < dm.regs.rdi.toNat + b.size) ∧
    46      ¬ (dm.regs.rdx.toNat ≤ x ∧ x < dm.regs.rdx.toNat + pb.size)
    47    hcs24 : 24 ≤ dm.regs.rsp.toNat
    48    hcs8 : dm.regs.rsp.toNat + 8 < 2 ^ 64

== ConAgua/Final/Twin.lean#L27-L29
    27  The prelude is free: `builtinPreludeE_run` gives *some* con-leche prelude `preC` the twin's prelude
    28  denotes, and con-leche's `preparePrelude` puts its records into the checked stream, so soundness
    29  holds whatever the prelude bytes are. The pins are free for the same reason as in con-leche.

== ConAgua/Checker/Pipeline.lean#L69-L72
    69  /-- What every stage may assume of the inputs: a 64-bit platform, both buffers below `2^63`
    70  bytes, every word array below `2^64` words. -/
    71  def InputsOK (b pb : ByteArray) (s64 : List Nat) : Prop :=
    72    System.Platform.numBits = 64 ∧ b.size < 2 ^ 63 ∧ pb.size < 2 ^ 63 ∧ ∀ n ∈ s64, n < 2 ^ 64

== scripts/check-asm.sh#L1-L12
     1  #!/usr/bin/env bash
     2  # Assemble and disassemble every program the compiler proof covers (the scanner, the `lit` store,
     3  # the arena walk, and the whole checker: the committed file `checker.s`, whose code the final
     4  # theorems are about, docs/design/asmfile.md) and check, instruction by instruction, that what `as`/`objdump` actually encode
     5  # agrees with what `asmText` (Kraken's AT&T printer) printed. This is the trusted-base check: the
     6  # printer and the assembler are *not* proved, so
     7  # `compile_correct` only holds of the real machine if their printed/assembled text means what
     8  # Kraken's instruction semantics says, and this is as close to checking that automatically as we
     9  # get. See DESIGN.md ("the compiler", lane `walk`) and docs/gaps/kraken-att-imul-three-operand.lean
    10  # (the mismatch this script would have caught before it was found by hand).
    11  #
    12  # Usage: scripts/check-asm.sh (from anywhere in the repo; rebuilds the emitters it needs).

== main.c#L148-L166
   148  /* The input: a nonempty regular file is mapped read-only;
   149     anything else (a pipe, a terminal, an empty file) or a file mmap refuses is read with `slurp`.
   150     The bytes `b` the theorem talks about are whatever the buffer holds: a mapped file that
   151     another process changes during the run changes them (and one truncated faults: a crash). */
   152  static uint8_t *read_input(const char *path, uint64_t *n) {
   153    int fd = open(path, O_RDONLY);
   154    if (fd < 0) fail(path, strerror(errno));
   155    struct stat st;
   156    if (fstat(fd, &st) == 0 && S_ISREG(st.st_mode) && st.st_size > 0) {
   157      uint8_t *buf = mmap(0, st.st_size, PROT_READ, MAP_PRIVATE, fd, 0);
   158      if (buf != MAP_FAILED) {
   159        close(fd);
   160        in_mapped = 1;
   161        *n = st.st_size;
   162        return buf;
   163      }
   164    }
   165    return slurp(fd, path, n);
   166  }

== ConAgua/Final/ThreadsFinal.lean#L125-L149
   125  /-- **What the threaded harness does** (trusted; the module doc lists it): entry 1 at `dm₀`
   126  returning at `st₀`, the buffer `B`, and the threads `ths`. -/
   127  structure ThreadsRun [Host] (b pb : ByteArray) (dm₀ : MachineData) (ra₀ : Word) (st₀ : MachineState)
   128      (B : Array Word) (ths : List ThreadM) : Prop where
   129    call₀ : AbiCall b pb dm₀ ra₀
   130    ret₀ : FirstReturn dm₀ (label abiStartAL) ra₀ st₀
   131    rdx₀ : st₀.data.regs.rdx = 0
   132    rax₀ : 9223372036854775808 ≤ st₀.data.regs.rax.toNat
   133    /-- the buffer: `OUT`'s first `len` words, `len` its word `1` -/
   134    bufw : ∀ i (h : i < B.size), rdW st₀.data.dmem (A (outAddr dm₀.regs.r8.toNat + 8 * i)) = some B[i]
   135    buflen : ∃ w, rdW st₀.data.dmem (A (outAddr dm₀.regs.r8.toNat + 8)) = some w ∧ w.toNat = B.size
   136    /-- the calls: the buffer in place, each thread on its region -/
   137    calls : ∀ t ∈ ths, ∀ i < t.n, BufCallH B (t.dm i) (t.ra i) ∧
   138      (t.dm i).regs.rdi.toNat = outAddr dm₀.regs.r8.toNat ∧ (t.dm i).regs.rcx.toNat = t.base ∧
   139      (t.dm i).regs.r8.toNat = t.blen
   140    zero : ∀ t ∈ ths, 0 < t.n → ∀ x, t.base ≤ x → x < t.base + t.blen → (t.dm 0).dmem.get? (A x) = some 0
   141    ret : ∀ t ∈ ths, ∀ i < t.n, FirstReturn (t.dm i) (label abiCheckBL) (t.ra i) (t.st i)
   142    acc : ∀ t ∈ ths, ∀ i < t.n, (t.st i).data.regs.rdx = 0 ∧ (t.st i).data.regs.rax = ACCEPT
   143    /-- route A: the buffer's words at each call's return -/
   144    kept : ∀ t ∈ ths, ∀ i < t.n, ∀ q (h : q < B.size),
   145      rdW (t.st i).data.dmem (A (outAddr dm₀.regs.r8.toNat + 8 * q)) = some B[q]
   146    next : ∀ t ∈ ths, ∀ i, i + 1 < t.n → ∀ x, t.base ≤ x → x < t.base + t.blen →
   147      (t.dm (i + 1)).dmem.get? (A x) = (t.st i).data.dmem.get? (A x)
   148    claimed : ∀ t ∈ ths, ∀ i < t.n, (t.dm i).regs.rdx < st₀.data.regs.rax - 9223372036854775808
   149    cover : ∀ j : Word, j < st₀.data.regs.rax - 9223372036854775808 → ∃ t ∈ ths, ∃ i < t.n, (t.dm i).regs.rdx = j

== ConAgua/Final/ThreadsFinal.lean#L16-L35
    16  **What the theorem trusts of the harness** (the hypotheses of `ThreadsRun`; beyond them, what
    17  `Final/Statement.lean` lists: Kraken's semantics, the assembler, linker and loader):
    18  
    19  * **Entry 1's call**: `ca_start_a` is called as `AbiCall` says (the input and pin buffers, a zero
    20    region, the 32 bytes of machine stack around `rsp`; `mmap` gives the stated memory facts).
    21  * **First return** (`FirstReturn`): the harness regains control, at each call's return address,
    22    in a state that has every property the machine is guaranteed to reach at that address
    23    (`abiA_outcome`'s and `abiB_outcome`'s posts).
    24  * **The buffer** is the first `len` words of `OUT`'s slot of entry 1's region at its return, `len`
    25    `OUT`'s word `1`, and stays in place: every thread's call is passed its address and sees the
    26    same words, before the call and at its return (**route A**: read-only, `mprotect`).
    27  * **Each thread's region** is its own (pthreads: the threads' regions are apart from each other,
    28    from the buffer and from every thread's stack window): zero at the thread's first call, and at
    29    each later call holding the bytes the previous call left. Each call is made as `BufCallH` says
    30    (the region mapped and large enough, the buffer apart from it, the return address and the
    31    32-byte stack window).
    32  * **The claim counter's coverage**: every claimed group index `j` (in `rdx`) is below `k`
    33    (`k = rax - 2^63` from entry 1), and every index below `k` is claimed by some thread.
    34  * The verdicts: entry 1 returns `rdx = 0`, `rax ≥ 2^63`; every call returns `rdx = 0`,
    35    `rax = ACCEPT`.

== ConAgua/Final/ThreadsVerdict.lean#L50-L89
    50  structure Entry1Fail [Host] (b pb : ByteArray) (dm₀ : MachineData) (ra₀ : Word) (st₀ : MachineState) :
    51      Prop where
    52    call₀ : AbiCall b pb dm₀ ra₀
    53    ret₀ : FirstReturn dm₀ (label abiStartAL) ra₀ st₀
    54    rdx₀ : st₀.data.regs.rdx = 2
    55  
    56  /-- **A thread's call `i` fails** (trusted; the module doc lists it): entry 1 at `dm₀` returning
    57  at `st₀`, the buffer `B`, and the thread `t`'s calls `0, …, i` (`ThreadsRun`'s fields for them),
    58  the calls before `i` accepting, call `i` returning `rdx = 2`. -/
    59  structure ThreadFail [Host] (b pb : ByteArray) (dm₀ : MachineData) (ra₀ : Word) (st₀ : MachineState)
    60      (B : Array Word) (t : ThreadM) (i : Nat) : Prop where
    61    call₀ : AbiCall b pb dm₀ ra₀
    62    ret₀ : FirstReturn dm₀ (label abiStartAL) ra₀ st₀
    63    rdx₀ : st₀.data.regs.rdx = 0
    64    rax₀ : 9223372036854775808 ≤ st₀.data.regs.rax.toNat
    65    /-- the buffer: `OUT`'s first `len` words, `len` its word `1` -/
    66    bufw : ∀ q (h : q < B.size), rdW st₀.data.dmem (A (outAddr dm₀.regs.r8.toNat + 8 * q)) = some B[q]
    67    buflen : ∃ w, rdW st₀.data.dmem (A (outAddr dm₀.regs.r8.toNat + 8)) = some w ∧ w.toNat = B.size
    68    /-- the calls: the buffer in place, on the thread's region -/
    69    calls : ∀ i' ≤ i, BufCallH B (t.dm i') (t.ra i') ∧
    70      (t.dm i').regs.rdi.toNat = outAddr dm₀.regs.r8.toNat ∧ (t.dm i').regs.rcx.toNat = t.base ∧
    71      (t.dm i').regs.r8.toNat = t.blen
    72    zero : ∀ x, t.base ≤ x → x < t.base + t.blen → (t.dm 0).dmem.get? (A x) = some 0
    73    ret : ∀ i' ≤ i, FirstReturn (t.dm i') (label abiCheckBL) (t.ra i') (t.st i')
    74    acc : ∀ i' < i, (t.st i').data.regs.rdx = 0 ∧ (t.st i').data.regs.rax = ACCEPT
    75    rdx : (t.st i).data.regs.rdx = 2
    76    /-- route A: the buffer's words at each accepting call's return -/
    77    kept : ∀ i' < i, ∀ q (h : q < B.size),
    78      rdW (t.st i').data.dmem (A (outAddr dm₀.regs.r8.toNat + 8 * q)) = some B[q]
    79    next : ∀ i', i' < i → ∀ x, t.base ≤ x → x < t.base + t.blen →
    80      (t.dm (i' + 1)).dmem.get? (A x) = (t.st i').data.dmem.get? (A x)
    81    claimed : ∀ i' ≤ i, (t.dm i').regs.rdx < st₀.data.regs.rax - 9223372036854775808
    82  
    83  /-- **The threaded harness reports a failure with the code `k`**: entry 1 failed with
    84  `rax = k`, or a thread's call `i` failed with `rax = k`. -/
    85  def ThreadsFail [Host] (b pb : ByteArray) (dm₀ : MachineData) (ra₀ : Word) (st₀ : MachineState)
    86      (k : Word) : Prop :=
    87    (Entry1Fail b pb dm₀ ra₀ st₀ ∧ k = st₀.data.regs.rax) ∨
    88    ∃ (B : Array Word) (t : ThreadM) (i : Nat), ThreadFail b pb dm₀ ra₀ st₀ B t i ∧
    89      k = (t.st i).data.regs.rax

== ConAgua/Final/ThreadsVerdict.lean#L24-L39
    24  **What the theorem trusts of the harness** (the hypotheses of `Entry1Fail` and `ThreadFail`;
    25  beyond them, what `Final/Statement.lean` lists: Kraken's semantics, the assembler, linker and
    26  loader):
    27  
    28  * **Entry 1's call**: `ca_start_a` is called as `AbiCall` says; **first return** (`FirstReturn`):
    29    the harness regains control at the return address in a state with every property the machine
    30    is guaranteed to reach there (`abiA_outcome`'s and `abiB_outcome`'s posts).
    31  * On a thread's failure (`ThreadFail`), for the thread's calls up to the failing call `i`, what
    32    `ThreadsRun` trusts: the buffer (`OUT`'s first `len` words at entry 1's return) stays in place
    33    and is passed to each call (route A: read-only, `mprotect`); the thread's region is its own,
    34    zero at the first call, and at each later call holding the bytes the previous call left; each
    35    call is made as `BufCallH` says; every claimed group index (in `rdx`) is below `k`
    36    (`k = rax - 2^63` from entry 1). Coverage of the group indices by the threads is not needed.
    37  * The verdicts: entry 1 returns `rdx = 2` (`Entry1Fail`), or `rdx = 0` and `rax ≥ 2^63`, the
    38    thread's calls before `i` return `rdx = 0`, `rax = ACCEPT`, and call `i` returns `rdx = 2`
    39    (`ThreadFail`). The harness reports the code `k` it read from that call's `rax`.

== ConAgua/Compiler/Main.lean#L27-L31
    27  /-- What the harness sees after `ca_enter` returns, against L's result. -/
    28  def OutcomeRel (G : Layout) : Except Err (List Word × Mem) → MachineData → Prop
    29    | .ok (rs, m'), s => s.regs.rdx = 0 ∧ ResOut G G.tab.nres rs s ∧ MemRel G m' s.dmem
    30    | .error .outOfFuel, _ => False
    31    | .error e, s => s.regs.rdx = 2 ∧ s.regs.rax = e.code

== ConAgua/L/Syntax.lean#L5-L15
     5  /-!
     6  # L: abstract syntax
     7  
     8  L is the small first-order language the checker is written in (see `DESIGN.md`, "The language L").
     9  Values are 64-bit words with wrapping arithmetic. A function has numbered locals, the first
    10  `nparams` of which are its parameters. Memory is a fixed set of arrays: byte arrays (the input
    11  buffer) and word arrays, each named by a static index, and a store of global word variables
    12  (`GVar`), also named by static indices. Expressions have no side effects and
    13  make no calls; a call is a statement. Conditions are a separate type, with short-circuit `&&`/`||`
    14  so that a guard such as `i < len && b[i] == c` cannot read out of bounds.
    15  -/

== ConAgua/Compiler/Main.lean#L774-L797
   774  /-- **The end-to-end compiler theorem** (`compile_correct_frame` without the memory frame): the
   775  caller's `rsp`, `rbp`, `r14`, `r15`, `rbx`, `r12`, `r13` are restored on every path, whatever
   776  registers the compiled functions use. -/

   786      (hra : rdW d.dmem (A d.regs.rsp.toNat) = some ra)
   787      (hcs : ∀ x, d.regs.rsp.toNat - 24 ≤ x → x < d.regs.rsp.toNat + 8 →
   788        (d.dmem.get? (A x)).isSome ∧ ¬ G.InStack x ∧ ¬ G.InArr x ∧ ¬ G.InTab x)
   789      (hcs24 : 24 ≤ d.regs.rsp.toNat) (hcs8 : d.regs.rsp.toNat + 8 < 2 ^ 64)

   791        ¬ G.InArr x ∧ (x < d.regs.rsp.toNat - 24 ∨ d.regs.rsp.toNat + 8 ≤ x))

   795          CalleeKept d.regs st.data.regs ∧
   796          (st.data.regs.rdx = 1 ∨ OutcomeRel G (run p N entry args m) st.data))
   797        d (label enterL) :=

== ConAgua/Arena/IndIface.lean#L296-L307
   296  /-- **A refinement of the twin's `op` by the L call `f(args)`**: from any memory satisfying `pre`
   297  against `a₀`, a returning run keeps the caller's locals, the twin's run succeeds, and `post`
   298  relates the memories before and after, the twin's state after, the L results and the twin's
   299  result. Every stub spec and every refinement of the stage has this shape. -/
   300  def RefAM {α : Type} [Inhabited α] (p : Prog) (f : FnName) (args : List Word)
   301      (pre : Mem → AState → Prop) (op : AM α)
   302      (post : Mem → Mem → AState → List Word → α → Prop) : Prop :=
   303    ∀ (n : Nat) (s₀ : St) (a₀ : AState), pre s₀.mem a₀ →
   304      ⦃fun s => s = s₀⦄ invoke p (exec p n) f args
   305      ⦃fun r s' => LocEq s' s₀ ∧ AM.ok op a₀ ∧
   306        post s₀.mem s'.mem (AM.st op a₀) r (AM.res op a₀); ⊤⦄
   307

== ConAgua/Checker/Entry.lean#L120-L127
   120  /-- `check()`: one of the parallel mode's entries, by the mode word; any other mode aborts. -/

== vendor/con-ron/ConRon/Arena/Main.lean#L154-L190
   154  def runPipelineHead :
   155      AM (Except (CheckError × Nat) (Frontend.PreludeIx × Frontend.StateD)) := do
   156    -- **The reserved-name pins, interned ONCE** (task #97-P6-4a): immediately
   157    -- after the state is made and before the prelude, so the scratch tier is
   158    -- closed and every pinned handle is persistent.
   159    internReservedPins
   160    match ← Frontend.builtinPreludeE with
   161    | .error e => pure (.error e)
   162    | .ok pre => pure (.ok (pre, ← Frontend.StateD.init))
   163  
   164  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/Run.lean:236-424 checkMain
   165  The pipeline AFTER the parse: `preparePrelude`, then **the fold** (task
   166  #97d), then the verdict number.  Shared verbatim by the pure seam and by the
   167  driver's interleaved loop, which is what makes the two the same computation.
   168  
   169  The verdict number is con-leche's own, "a property of the INPUT"
   170  (`ConLeche/Driver/Run.lean`'s `checkMain`): the records the parse produced, which no later step
   171  moves.  The fold's own environment is discarded — an accept is the
   172  statement, not the environment.
   173  
   174  `internAllPins` runs BEFORE the fold and while the scratch tier is still off,
   175  which is what DESIGN §8.6 P2d means by "at startup": every pinned datum is in
   176  the persistent cons table before any declaration's check can intern one into
   177  a tier that is about to vanish. -/
   178  def runPipelineTail (mode : CheckMode) (pins : List NatOpPinSet)
   179      (pre : Frontend.PreludeIx) (r : Frontend.ParseResultD) :
   180      AM (Except CheckError Nat) := do
   181    -- The verdict number is read HERE, before the fold, so that `r` dies at
   182    -- `preparePrelude` instead of being pinned across the whole check (DESIGN
   183    -- §8.4: decide the rare branch, and read what a later line needs, BEFORE
   184    -- the expensive step).
   185    let records := r.decls.size
   186    let ds ← Frontend.preparePrelude pre r.decls
   187    let ipins ← internAllPins pins
   188    match ← installThenCheck mode ipins ds with
   189    | .error (e, n) => pure (.error (atDecl e n))
   190    | .ok _ => pure (.ok records)

    69  /-- Word expressions. Reading an array can fail (out of bounds); nothing else can. -/
    70  inductive Expr where
    71    | const (w : Word)
    72    | var (x : Var)
    73    | bin (op : BinOp) (a b : Expr)

    76    /-- Word `i` of word array `a`. -/

    80    /-- The length (in elements) of word array `a`. -/
    81    | len64 (a : ArrId)

    83    | cmpw (c : Cmp) (a b : Expr)

    85    | ldc (d : List UInt8) (i : Expr)
    86    /-- The global variable `g`. -/
    87    | glob (g : GVar)

    89    `a + tierOff` for `t & 1 = 1`; lane tierarr). -/
    90    | ld64t (a : ArrId) (t i : Expr)
    91    /-- The length of tier `t` of the tiered array `a`. -/
    92    | len64t (a : ArrId) (t : Expr)
    93    /-- The little-endian word of the bytes `i, …, i + 7` of `s` (lane blkcopy). -/
    94    | ld8x8 (s : BSrc) (i : Expr)

== ConAgua/L/Syntax.lean#L117-L153
   117  /-- Statements. -/
   118  inductive Stmt where
   119    | skip
   120    /-- `x := e` -/
   121    | set (x : Var) (e : Expr)
   122    /-- `a.u8[i] := e` (the low byte of `e`) -/
   123    | st8 (a : ArrId) (i e : Expr)
   124    /-- `a.u64[i] := e` -/
   125    | st64 (a : ArrId) (i e : Expr)
   126    | seq (s t : Stmt)
   127    | ite (c : Cond) (s t : Stmt)
   128    /-- `while c { s }`. Each iteration costs one unit of fuel. -/
   129    | while (c : Cond) (s : Stmt)
   130    /-- Leave the innermost loop. -/
   131    | brk
   132    /-- Return from the function with the values `es` (usually one). -/
   133    | ret (es : List Expr)
   134    /-- `(x₀, x₁, …) := f(args)`: `xᵢ` gets the callee's `i`-th result, `0` if it returned fewer.
   135    A call costs one unit of fuel. -/
   136    | call (xs : List Var) (f : FnName) (args : List Expr)
   137    /-- Stop the whole program with an error (Rust's `panic!`, an overflow check, …) whose code is
   138    the value of `e` (`Err.abort`): the low two bits are the class (`0` other, `1` reject, `2`
   139    decline), the rest a reason. A bare `abort` is `abort 0`. -/
   140    | abort (e : Expr)
   141    /-- `g := e` for a global variable `g`. -/
   142    | gset (g : GVar) (e : Expr)
   143    /-- `a⟨t⟩.u64[i] := e`: word `i` of tier `t` of the tiered array `a`. -/
   144    | st64t (a : ArrId) (t i e : Expr)
   145    /-- `copy D[di ..] := S[si ..] for n`: words `si, …, si + n - 1` of `S` to `di, …` of `D`, in
   146    ascending order; bounds checked once, before anything is written (lane blkcopy). -/
   147    | copy64 (d : WArr) (di : Expr) (s : WArr) (si n : Expr)
   148    /-- `copy D[di ..] := S.u8[si ..] for n`: the bytes zero-extended into words. -/
   149    | copy8w (d : WArr) (di : Expr) (s : BSrc) (si n : Expr)
   150    /-- `x := scan S.u8[i .. e] until c`: the first `j` in `[i, e)` with `c[S[j]] ≠ 0`, else `e`
   151    (`c`: a 256-byte class table, constant data). -/
   152    | scan8 (x : Var) (s : BSrc) (i e : Expr) (c : List UInt8)
   153    deriving Repr, Inhabited

== ConAgua/L/Syntax.lean#L155-L165
   155  /-- A function: `nparams` parameters, `nlocals ≥ nparams` locals (params first, the rest start
   156  at `0`), and a body. Falling off the end of the body (or a `break` outside a loop) returns no
   157  values (so every result the caller reads is `0`). -/

   159    nparams : Nat
   160    nlocals : Nat
   161    body : Stmt
   162    deriving Repr, Inhabited
   163  
   164  /-- A program: its functions, by name. The first binding of a name wins. -/
   165  abbrev Prog := List (FnName × FunDecl)

== ConAgua/L/Notation.lean#L11-L62
    11  # L: concrete syntax
    12  
    13  A Rust-like surface for writing L functions by hand:
    14  
    15  ```
    16  lfn (b_dummy, j) locals (c) {
    17    while j < len(IN.u8) {
    18      c := IN.u8[j];
    19      if c == '"' { return j } else { j += 1 }
    20    };
    21    return 0
    22  }
    23  ```
    24  
    25  * `lfn (params) locals (more) { body }` is a term of type `L.FunDecl`. Variable names resolve to
    26    local indices in declaration order (parameters first).
    27  * `A.u8[i]` / `A.u64[i]` read byte / word array `A`, where `A` is a Lean constant of type
    28    `L.ArrId`; `len(A.u8)` / `len(A.u64)` are the lengths. Stores are `A.u8[i] := e`.
    29  * `R[i].f` reads field `f` of record `i` of the record layout `R : L.Record` (a Lean constant;
    30    the field is the constant `R.f : L.Field`), `R[i].f := e` writes it: the word
    31    `i * stride + f.off` of the word array `R.arr` (`L/Records.lean`).
    32  * `A⟨t⟩[i]` reads word `i` of tier `t` of the tiered word array `A` (`L.tierA A t`: `A`, or
    33    `A + tierOff` when `t & 1 = 1`); `len(A⟨t⟩)` is that tier's length, `A⟨t⟩[i] := e` writes it,
    34    and `R⟨t⟩[i].f` / `R⟨t⟩[i].f := e` are records in a tiered array (lane tierarr).
    35  * The node stores' records (`L/TRec.lean`, the stores in `Arena/StoreFields.lean`; lane tieracc):
    36    `R⟨t, i⟩.f` is field `f` of node `i` of tier `t` of the store `R : L.TRec` (`R⟨t, i⟩` a one-word
    37    column), `R⟦h⟧.f` / `R⟦h⟧` the node the handle word `h` names, `R⟨t⟩.count` the node count of
    38    tier `t`, `⟦h⟧.tier` / `⟦h⟧.idx` a handle's tier bit and index; `R⟨t, i⟩.f := e` writes a field
    39    (the store library only).
    40  * `⦃x⦄.tier`, `⦃x⦄.idx`, `⦃x⦄.base` are the tier (bit 40), the index (the low 40 bits) and the
    41    tier's base address (`(x >> 40) << 40`) of a tier-tagged address `x`, and `A⦃x⦄` reads the word
    42    at the tagged address `x` of the tiered word array `A` (`A⟨⦃x⦄.tier⟩[⦃x⦄.idx]`). The limb
    43    pool's slices are named by such addresses: the tier is `1` for a slice of the scratch tier (open
    44    while the arena's scratch flag is set) and `0` otherwise (lane tierpool). A
    45    store's tier must be simple, so a writer decodes the tier and base of its top once into locals
    46    and indexes relative to the base: `t := ⦃top⦄.tier; b := ⦃top⦄.base; … A⟨t⟩[top + j - b] := e`
    47    (for a tier-0 top this is exactly `A[top + j]`, out-of-bounds aborts included). This macro is
    48    the one place that fixes the encoding.
    49  * `D.c8[i]` reads byte `i` of the constant byte string `D : List UInt8` (a Lean constant);
    50    `len(D.c8)` is its length (a constant).
    51  * Literals: numbers, characters (`'{'` is `123`), and `⟪t⟫` for any Lean term of type `Word`.
    52  * An identifier that is not a local names a global variable: a Lean constant `g : L.GVar`
    53    (`abbrev HTOP : L.GVar := ⟨3⟩`). `g` reads it, `g := e`, `g += e`, `g -= e` write it.
    54  * Operators `+ - * & | ^ << >>` (wrapping, as in Rust's `wrapping_*`), `mulhi(a, b)` (the high
    55    word of the 128-bit product), `u64(a < b)` (a comparison as `1`/`0`, Rust's `(a < b) as u64`),
    56    comparisons
    57    `== != < <= > >=` (unsigned) and `<ₛ ≤ₛ` (signed), and short-circuit `&& || !`.
    58  * Statements are separated by `;`: `x := e`, `x += e`, `x -= e`, `x := call f(e, …)`,
    59    `(x, y, …) := call f(e, …)` (several results), `if c { … } else { … }` (with `else if`),
    60    `while c { … }`, `break`, `return e`, `return (e, e', …)`, `abort`, `abort R`, `fail R`, `skip`, and `⟪t⟫` for a
    61    named block `t : L.Stmt` (see `lblk`; a block written with other variables than a prefix of
    62    the enclosing ones is an error).

== ConAgua/L/Semantics.lean#L7-L21
     7  /-!
     8  # L: semantics
     9  
    10  The meaning of an L program is a Lean function into the monad `M := StateT St (Except Err)`.
    11  It is executable (`#eval`), and it is what `vcgen` steps through in a proof.
    12  
    13  * `St` is the memory (`Mem`: the byte arrays and the word arrays) plus the current frame's locals.
    14  * `Err` is every way a run can fail. None of them is a result: a result is a list of words
    15    returned by the function, so "ran out of fuel" or "read out of bounds" can never read as "accept".
    16  * Fuel. `exec p n` is the `n`-th Kleene iterate of the one-step interpreter `step p`:
    17    `exec p 0` throws `outOfFuel`, and `exec p (n+1) = step p (exec p n)`. `step p k` interprets a
    18    statement by structural recursion and hands the next loop iteration and every callee body to
    19    `k`. So fuel bounds the nesting of loop iterations and calls along a path. A partial-correctness
    20    triple (exception post `⊤`) is proved by induction on `n` and never mentions fuel.
    21  -/

== ConAgua/L/Semantics.lean#L45-L55
    45  /-- The ways a run can fail. -/
    46  inductive Err where
    47    /-- The fuel (nesting of loop iterations and calls) ran out. -/
    48    | outOfFuel
    49    /-- An array access out of bounds, or to an array that does not exist. -/
    50    | oob
    51    /-- A call to an undefined function. -/
    52    | noFun (f : FnName)
    53    /-- An `abort e` statement, with the value `k` of `e`: the error's code (`Stmt.abort`). -/
    54    | abort (k : Word)
    55    deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited

== ConAgua/L/Semantics.lean#L361-L368
   361  /-- The interpreter with `n` units of fuel. -/
   362  def exec (p : Prog) : Nat → Stmt → M Sig
   363    | 0, _ => throw .outOfFuel
   364    | n + 1, s => step p (exec p n) s
   365  
   366  /-- Run function `f` of `p` on memory `m`: its results and the final memory. -/
   367  def run (p : Prog) (fuel : Nat) (f : FnName) (vs : List Word) (m : Mem) : Except Err (List Word × Mem) :=
   368    ((invoke p (exec p fuel) f vs).run { mem := m, loc := Locals.init [] }).map fun (r, s) => (r, s.mem)

== ConAgua/L/Semantics.lean#L25-L32
    25  /-- The memory: a fixed set of byte arrays and word arrays, indexed by `ArrId`, and the global
    26  variables. The arrays' lengths are fixed for the run (a growable vector is a fixed-capacity array
    27  plus a length kept in a word). Every global variable has a value (`0` unless written). -/
    28  structure Mem where
    29    bytes : Array (Array UInt8) := #[]
    30    words : Array (Array Word) := #[]
    31    glob : GVar → Word := fun _ => 0
    32    deriving Inhabited

== ConAgua/L/Syntax.lean#L28-L35
    28  /-- **Tiered arrays** (lane tierarr). Tier `1` of word array `a` is word array `a + tierOff`;
    29  an access with a run-time tier word `t` uses `tierA a t` (the tier is masked: `t & 1`). So a
    30  program sees one array per tier, as con-ron's per-tier tables, and the compiler finds tier `1`'s
    31  descriptor at a fixed distance from tier `0`'s. -/
    32  @[expose] def tierOff : Nat := 256
    33  
    34  /-- The array of tier `t` of the tiered array `a`. -/
    35  @[expose] def tierA (a : ArrId) (t : UInt64) : ArrId := a + tierOff * (t &&& 1).toNat

== ConAgua/L/Arrays.lean#L34-L56
    34  @[expose, reducible] def tier1 (a : ArrId) : ArrId := a + tierOff
    35  
    36  /-- The two tiers of the tiered array `a`. -/
    37  @[expose, reducible] def tiers (a : ArrId) : List ArrId := [a, tier1 a]
    38  
    39  theorem and_one_cases' (t : Word) : (t &&& 1).toNat = 0 ∨ (t &&& 1).toNat = 1 := by
    40    rw [UInt64.toNat_and, UInt64.toNat_one, Nat.and_one_is_mod]; omega
    41  
    42  @[simp] theorem tierA_zero (a : ArrId) : tierA a 0 = a := rfl
    43  
    44  theorem tierA_one_eq (a : ArrId) : tierA a 1 = tier1 a := rfl
    45  
    46  /-- Tier `t` of `a` is `a` or `tier1 a`. -/
    47  theorem tierA_eq_or (a : ArrId) (t : Word) : tierA a t = a ∨ tierA a t = tier1 a := by
    48    rcases and_one_cases' t with h | h <;> simp [tierA, tier1, h]
    49  
    50  /-- **The arrays `tierA a t` can be are `tiers a`.** -/
    51  theorem tierA_mem_tiers (a : ArrId) (t : Word) : tierA a t ∈ tiers a := by
    52    rcases tierA_eq_or a t with h | h <;> simp [tiers, h]
    53  
    54  /-- An array that is neither tier of `a` is not `tierA a t`. -/
    55  theorem tierA_ne {a b : ArrId} (h : b ∉ tiers a) (t : Word) : tierA a t ≠ b := fun e =>
    56    h (e ▸ tierA_mem_tiers a t)

== ConAgua/L/TRec.lean#L7-L31
     7  /-!
     8  # Tiered store records (surface syntax)
     9  
    10  A node store of the arena (`Arena/StoreFields.lean` lists them) keeps, per tier, an array of
    11  records of `w` words, and the node count of each tier in a control word. Code outside the store
    12  library reaches them only through the accessors below, written in L as
    13  
    14  * `R⟨t, i⟩.f`: field `f` of node `i` of tier `t` (`R⟨t, i⟩` for a one-word column);
    15  * `R⟦h⟧.f`, `R⟦h⟧`: the same for the node a handle word `h` names (tier bit 27, index the low 27
    16    bits);
    17  * `R⟨t⟩.count`: the node count of tier `t`;
    18  * `R⟨t, i⟩.f := e`: a field store (the store library's pushes only).
    19  
    20  They expand (`Notation.lean`) to the builders `TRec.ld`, `TRec.st`, `TRec.cntE` of this file,
    21  which fix the **layout** in one place: one tiered word array per store (lane tierswitch; tier
    22  `t` of array `a` is array `L.tierA a t`), node `i` of tier `t` at
    23  `arr⟨t⟩[i * w ..]`, the count at `CTL[ca + t]`. Proofs see the named words `TRec.ad`, `tfld`, `tcnt`.
    24  
    25  **Packed records** (lane memlay, `hi ≠ 0`): field `0` and field `hi` (two handle words, below
    26  `2^32`) share word `0` of the record, field `0` in bits 0–31 and field `hi` in bits 32–63; the
    27  other fields `f` follow in words `1 ‥` (`f`, or `f - 1` above `hi`), whole. A field's word is
    28  `TRec.wd`, its address `TRec.ad`; a load extracts the half (`TRec.ex`: `x & 0xFFFFFFFF`,
    29  `x >> 32`). Records are written once, whole, by the store library's pushes (the combined word
    30  `f₀ | f_hi << 32`); `TRec.st` stores a whole word (unpacked fields only).
    31  -/

== ConAgua/L/Notation.lean#L97-L98
    97  /-- `le64!(A.u8, i)`: the little-endian word of the bytes `i … i + 7` (`D.c8` for constant bytes). -/
    98  syntax "le64!" "(" ident ", " lexpr ")" : lexpr

== ConAgua/L/Notation.lean#L149-L155
   149  /-- `x := scan!(A.u8, i, e, C)`: the first `j ∈ [i, e)` whose byte is in the class `C` (a Lean
   150  constant: a 256-byte table), else `e` (`D.c8` for constant bytes; lane blkcopy). -/
   151  syntax ident " := " "scan!" "(" ident ", " lexpr ", " lexpr ", " ident ")" : lstmt
   152  /-- `copy!(D, di, S, si, n)`: `D[di + j] := S[si + j]` for `j < n` (`S` a word array `B.u64` or bytes
   153  `B.u8`/`B.c8`; `D⟨t⟩`, `S⟨t⟩` for tiered word arrays; lane blkcopy). -/
   154  syntax "copy!" "(" ident (noWs "⟨" lexpr "⟩")? ", " lexpr ", " ident (noWs "⟨" lexpr "⟩")? ", " lexpr ", "
   155    lexpr ")" : lstmt

== ConAgua/L/Semantics.lean#L145-L164
   145  /-- The little-endian word of the bytes `k, …, k + 7` of `b` (as the machine's 8-byte load
   146  reads them: Kraken's `Nat.ofBytes`). -/
   147  def le64 (b : Array UInt8) (k : Nat) : Word :=
   148    UInt64.ofNat (((List.range 8).map fun j => b[k + j]!).foldr (fun x acc => acc * 256 + x.toNat) 0)
   149  
   150  /-- `D[di + j] := S[si + j]` for `j < n`, ascending (each word read after the writes before it). -/
   151  def Mem.copy64 (m : Mem) (d : ArrId) (di : Word) (s : ArrId) (si : Word) : Nat → Mem
   152    | 0 => m
   153    | n + 1 => (m.set64 d di ((m.arr64 s)[si.toNat]!)).copy64 d (di + 1) s (si + 1) n
   154  
   155  /-- `D[di + j] := b[si + j]` (zero-extended) for `j < n`, ascending. -/
   156  def Mem.copy8w (m : Mem) (d : ArrId) (di : Word) (b : Array UInt8) (si : Word) : Nat → Mem
   157    | 0 => m
   158    | n + 1 => (m.set64 d di (b[si.toNat]!).toUInt64).copy8w d (di + 1) b (si + 1) n
   159  
   160  /-- The first `j` in `[i, e)` with `c[b[j]] ≠ 0`, else `e` (for `i ≤ e`). -/
   161  def scanN (b : Array UInt8) (c : List UInt8) (i e : Nat) : Nat :=
   162    if i < e then (if c[(b[i]!).toNat]! ≠ 0 then i else scanN b c (i + 1) e) else i
   163  termination_by e - i
   164  

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L636-L647
   636  /-- `copy D[di ..] := S[si ..] for n`: the source checked and pointed at by `rcx`, the
   637  destination by `rdx`, the end of the source in temporary `0`, then 6 instructions per word. -/
   638  def copy64Code (ctx : Ctx) (path : Path) (d : WArr) (di : Expr) (s : WArr) (si n : Expr) : Program :=
   639    (warrDesc ctx .rcx s).1 ++ [movRM .rax (mb (warrDesc ctx .rcx s).2 (ctx.tab.len64 s.arr))] ++
   640    lenChk ctx si n ++ wordPtr ctx .rcx (warrDesc ctx .rcx s).2 s.arr si ++
   641    (warrDesc ctx .rdx d).1 ++ [movRM .rax (mb (warrDesc ctx .rdx d).2 (ctx.tab.len64 d.arr))] ++
   642    lenChk ctx di n ++ wordPtr ctx .rdx (warrDesc ctx .rdx d).2 d.arr di ++
   643    [i64 (.mov (.reg (rr .rax)) (opnd ctx n)),
   644     i64 (.shl (.reg (rr .rax)) (.imm8 (.int64 (Int64.ofInt 3)))),
   645     i64 (.add (.reg (rr .rax)) (oR .rcx)), movMR (ctx.tmp 0) .rax,
   646     i64 (.cmp (.reg (rr .rcx)) (oM (ctx.tmp 0))), jccL .nc (ctx.lbl path "X")] ++
   647    copy64Loop (ctx.lbl path "L") (ctx.tmp 0) ++ [.label (ctx.lbl path "X")]

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L669-L676
   669  /-- The loop of `scan8`: per byte the byte, its class (constant data at `[r15 + off]`) and the
   670  tests, 7 instructions. -/
   671  def scanLoop (Lb Xb : Label) (off : Int) (eo : Operand .W64) : Program :=
   672    [.label Lb,
   673     i64 (.movzx (.reg (rr .rdx)) (w' := .W8) (.mem (mbi .rcx .rax .W8))),
   674     i64 (.movzx (.reg (rr .rdx)) (w' := .W8) (.mem (tblAddr off))),
   675     i64 (.cmp (.reg (rr .rdx)) (oI 0)), jccL .nz Xb,
   676     i64 (.add (.reg (rr .rax)) (oI 1)), i64 (.cmp (.reg (rr .rax)) eo), jccL .c Lb]

== ConAgua/L/TRec.lean#L93-L97
    93  /-- The tier of a handle word: bit 27. -/
    94  @[expose] def tierE (h : Expr) : Expr := .bin .and (.bin .shr h (.const 27)) (.const 1)
    95  
    96  /-- The node index of a handle word: the low 27 bits. -/
    97  @[expose] def idxE (h : Expr) : Expr := .bin .and h (.const 134217727)

== ConAgua/Arena/StoreFields.lean#L11-L33
    11  # The store records: one accessor per field, one evaluation lemma per accessor (lane tieracc)
    12  
    13  Every node store of the arena keeps its records in a word array and its node counts in `CTL`
    14  (`L/TRec.lean`). This file is the **only** place outside the store library that knows the
    15  layout:
    16  
    17  * **The stores** (`LIT`, `APP`, …, `LVLS`) and their one-word columns (`APP_DER`, …, `FVAR_LP`), as
    18    `L.TRec` values, with a constant per field (`APP.f`, `APP.a`, …). L code reads them as
    19    `APP⟨t, i⟩.f`, `APP⟦h⟧.a`, `APP⟨t⟩.count` (`L/Notation.lean`).
    20  * **The proof accessors** `tfld m R t i f` (field `f` of node `i` of tier `t`) and `tcnt m R t`
    21    (the node count of tier `t`), and the handle decoders `tierW`, `idxW`.
    22  * **One evaluation lemma per accessor**: `evalE_tld` / `tld_eq` (pass both to `vcgen`, as
    23    `ld64`), `evalE_cnt` / `tcntM_eq`, `evalE_tierE`, `evalE_idxE`, and the pure forms
    24    `Expr.pval_tld`, `Expr.pval_cntE`, … (`lang_grind`); the frame lemmas `tfld_set64_ne`,
    25    `tcnt_set64_ne`, `tfld_setG`, ….
    26  
    27  Proofs outside the store library state models and relations with `tfld` and `tcnt` and never
    28  unfold them (`TRec.ad` stays folded). The layout (one tiered array per store, lane
    29  `tierswitch`: tier `t` of array `a` is `tierA a t`) lives in `L/TRec.lean`, the definitions and
    30  lemma proofs here, and the store library.
    31  
    32  The array and control-word ids below are the memory map's (`AREC` = `APP.arr`, …): each store
    33  file's `abbrev` must agree, `StoreFieldsCheck.lean` checks it.

== ConAgua/Arena/ConsLib.lean#L206-L215
   206  /-! ## The slot layout (KSTP)
   207  
   208  Each tier has its own slot array `sa⟨t⟩` (lane tierswitch; con-ron's per-tier tables). Its words
   209  `0` and `1` hold `n - SN0` (`n` the slot count, a multiple of 8) and `o`, the table's offset (`0`:
   210  nothing writes it); the table starts at word `r = 2 + o`. Slot `j` is the two words `r + 2 j` (the
   211  value: `0` free, `B t + i + 1` node `i`) and `r + 2 j + 1` (the key word). The table grows at load
   212  3/4 (con-ron's `HashMap2`) and **in place** (lane memlay): it doubles where it is (`kgrowB`), so no
   213  old copy of it stays resident, and the growth aborts if the array cannot hold the doubled table.
   214  A fresh array (all zero) is a table of `SN0` slots at offset `0`: a small run touches only the
   215  array's first words.

== ConAgua/Arena/ConsLib.lean#L486-L491
   486  /-- The growth test: the tier grows when its node count `c + 1` passes 3/4 of its slot count
   487  `g + SN0` (`(g + SN0) * 3 < (c + 1) * 4`; con-ron's `HashMap2` load factor `LOAD_NUM/LOAD_DEN`). -/
   488  def cpGrowIf (C : ConsSch) : Stmt :=
   489    .ite (.cmp .ult (.bin .mul (.bin .add (.var (gO C + 1)) (.const SN0)) (.const 3))
   490        (.bin .mul (.bin .add (.var (2 + C.np)) (.const 1)) (.const 4)))
   491      (kgrowBlk C) .skip

== ConAgua/Arena/ConsLib.lean#L463-L469
   463  /-- **The growth of tier `t`, in place** (con-ron's `HashMap2::try_resize` doubles into a new
   464  table and frees the old one; here the table doubles where it is, so no old copy stays resident):
   465  the slot count doubles, the new upper half is zeroed, every live slot of the old half is marked,
   466  then each marked entry is re-inserted from its home in the doubled table (linear probing past
   467  the live unmarked slots; a marked slot met on the way is swapped and re-inserted next: absl's
   468  in-place rehash). Aborts if the array cannot hold the doubled table. Template variables
   469  `t n2 n H Q ob nb x e v q h j d bt` (`t` the push's tier, the others from `gO`). -/

== ConAgua/Arena/SlotGrow.lean#L41-L44
    41  /-- The home slot of hash `h` among `n`: con-ron's multiply-xor finaliser, then the high word
    42  of the product with `n` (Lemire's range reduction) in place of the power-of-two mask. -/
    43  def homeW (h n : Word) : Word :=
    44    UInt64.ofNat (((h * golden) ^^^ ((h * golden) >>> 32)).toNat * n.toNat / 2 ^ 64)

== ConAgua/Arena/Scratch.lean#L18-L37
    18  /-!
    19  # The scratch tier's lifecycle in L: open and drop without zeroing a slot
    20  
    21  con-ron's arena brackets every declaration check with `enterScratch` (open the scratch tier of all
    22  four stores, clear the walk memos) and `dropScratch` (`flushCaches`, then close the scratch tier
    23  and truncate it). In L the 19 tables keep their scratch tier as tier 1 of their slot and record
    24  arrays (`StoreLib.lean`); a slot of tier 1 holds `B + i + 1` for node `i`, with the **slot base**
    25  `B = CTL[62]` (`SCB`), and reads free at or below `B` (`slotV`). So emptying the scratch tier of
    26  every table is O(1) per table:
    27  
    28  * `scratch_reset(f)`: `B += 2^32`, the scratch flag `CTL[1] := f`, and the 19 tier-1 node
    29    counts `CTL[ca + 1] := 0`. Every old scratch slot holds at most `B + 2^27` and reads free
    30    against the new base; no slot is written. Once every `2^30` resets (`B ≥ 2^62`) the base wraps:
    31    the 19 scratch slot tables are zeroed and `B` restarts at `0` (con-ron's `clear` at
    32    `EPOCH_MAX`), so `B < 2^62 + 2^32` always holds.
    33  * `scratch_enter()`: `scratch_reset(1)` and the four walk memos' `clear` (epoch bumps).
    34  * `scratch_drop()`: `flush_caches()` (`CoreCaches.lean`, the per-declaration caches), then
    35    `scratch_reset(0)`.
    36  
    37  The refinement (`enterScratch`/`dropScratch` under `ArenaD`) is `ScratchRefine.lean`.

== ConAgua/Arena/MemoLib.lean#L19-L46
    19  /-!
    20  # The memo library: per-call memo tables with two-word keys and epoch stamps
    21  
    22  con-ron's arena keeps six per-call memos keyed `(EIdx × Nat)` (`inst1C`, `instLC`, `liftC`,
    23  `abs1C`, `inst1LC`, `instLPC`), two keyed `EIdx` (`bvarBC`, `fvarBC`) and two level ones
    24  (`Arena/Monad.lean`'s `Memos`); con-ron's Rust keeps them in `HashMap2` (`ron/hashmap2.rs`): open
    25  addressing, linear probing, an **epoch stamp** per slot so that `clear` is `epoch += 1`.
    26  
    27  A memo here is a **schema** `MemoSch`: a word array `arr` and a `CTL` index `cs` (`CTL[cs]` is the
    28  live stamp minus one, `CTL[cs + 1]` the live count). Four words per slot: the stamp, the key's two
    29  words, the value. A one-word key (`bvarBC`) is the two-word key with second word `0`. Slot `j` is
    30  **live** iff its stamp is `CTL[cs] + 1`; anything else is free space, so all-zero memory is an
    31  empty memo.
    32  
    33  The L code is **generic in the schema**: `memoFindG S`, `memoPutG S`, `memoClearG S` are Lean
    34  functions producing L functions with the schema's array and `CTL` words spliced in (`S.arr.u64[…]`,
    35  `CTL.u64[⟪S.cs⟫]`), and their `vcgen` specs are proved once, for a variable schema. An instance is
    36  three entries of the program (`("bm_find", memoFindG bmSch)`, …) and no proof.
    37  
    38  * `X_find(k1, k2)`: the probe from `homeW (k1 ^ (k2 << 32) ^ (k2 >> 32) * golden)`, returning
    39    `(found, slot, steps)`. Both halves of `k2` enter the hash: banked memos (`MemoBank.genW`), the
    40    eager bit and `rrSch` keep a second component in `k2`'s high half (lane `rfhash`: with only
    41    `k2 << 32` it was shifted out, and all banks' entries for one `k1` shared one probe cluster).
    42  * `X_put(k1, k2, v, fd, j)`: given the probe's `fd`, `j` **on the current memory**, write the
    43    value (and on a miss, the stamp and the key, growing the table past 3/4 load, con-ron's `HashMap2` load factor). Callers probe right
    44    before (`set` = `find; put`); a walk that recursed since its first probe probes again.
    45  * `X_clear()`: `CTL[cs] += 1`, `CTL[cs + 1] := 0`, aborting where the stamp would wrap.
    46  -/

== ConAgua/Arena/Pool.lean#L10-L29
    10  /-!
    11  # The limb pool: layout, abstraction, invariant
    12  
    13  con-ron's `ron::Nat` (`crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/nat.rs`) is a `Vec<u64>` of little-endian
    14  limbs with no trailing zero limb. In L there are no vectors: every number lives in ONE word array,
    15  the limb pool `POOL`, as a slice `(o, l)` (offset, length). The pool grows at the top: word 0 of
    16  the control array `CTL` holds the top `T`; `[0, T)` is in use, `[T, len(POOL))` is free. A
    17  function that makes a number appends its limbs at `T` and moves `T` up; nothing below `T` is
    18  ever written again, so every slice handed out stays valid (the frame is `Agree`).
    19  
    20  * abstraction: `pv p o l` is the number the slice `(o, l)` of the pool array `p` denotes,
    21    `Σ_{i<l} p[o+i] * 2^(64 i)`;
    22  * normal form: `Norm p o l`: the slice has no trailing zero limb (con-ron's `Nat.WF`), so equal
    23    numbers have equal slices up to position;
    24  * invariant of the pool (`PoolOK`): `T ≤ len(POOL) < 2^64` and `CTL` has its word.
    25  
    26  All of this is stated over the pool *array* `p : Array Word` and Lean `Nat` positions, and the
    27  lemmas are guarded equations about the named functions `pv`, `xv`, `lv`, registered for
    28  `grind` with multi-patterns that bind every variable (DESIGN.md, "Proof recipe").
    29  -/

== ConAgua/Compiler/Abi.lean#L8-L35
     8  # The entry stubs (lane `abi`)
     9  
    10  The harness's whole job shrinks to: map a zero region, hand over the two input buffers, call
    11  `ca_start(in, in_len, pins, pins_len, base, base_len)` once. `ca_start` is the sequential driver
    12  (`parStub`, below): it calls entry 1 and then entry 2 on the same region. Both go through the
    13  setup stub `ca_setup` (`abiStub`, an internal label; the argument registers as `ca_start`'s),
    14  emitted before the trampoline, which sets up inside the region everything the harness used to lay
    15  out (`L.Compiler.Tab`), then tail-jumps into the trampoline `ca_enter(T, fuel)`:
    16  
    17  * System V arguments: `rdi`/`rsi` = the input bytes (byte array `0`), `rdx`/`rcx` = the pin-data
    18    bytes (byte array `1`; ignored if the program has one byte array), `r8` = `base`, `r9` =
    19    `base_len`. Returns `rax`/`rdx` as `ca_enter` does.
    20  * If `base_len < abiNeed`, or if `in_len` or `pins_len` is `2^63` or more (the top bit of `rsi`
    21    or `rcx` set: `cmp r, 0; jl`), it returns at once with `rdx = 1` (resources exhausted; never
    22    accept). So a run that gets past the stub has both buffers below `2^63` bytes, which the
    23    refinements assume (`InputsOK`).
    24  * The region is a static partition into `abiSlot`-byte slots (no allocator; the pages that are
    25    never touched never become real): slot `0` is the table (`T = base`), slot `1` the L stack
    26    (`abiStack` bytes at its bottom), then one slot per byte array `2, …, nb - 1` and per word array.
    27    Each array starts at its slot's start; its length is `abiSlot` bytes, resp. `abiWords` words.
    28  * The constant data is written into the table by immediate stores (no `.rodata` read); the result
    29    area and the global variables are the region's zeros.
    30  * The fuel is `2^62 - 1` (`compile_correct` takes any `N < 2^62`).
    31  
    32  Nothing here is trusted: `sim_abiStub` (`ConAgua/Compiler/AbiSim.lean`) runs the stub on the
    33  machine, `abiLayout_ok` and `abi_memRel` (`ConAgua/Final/Abi.lean`) show that it establishes
    34  `Layout.Ok`/`MemRel` for the partition, and `abi_harness` gives `compile_correct`'s premises at
    35  the trampoline. -/

    28  namespace L
    29  
    30  /-- **The checker's arrays.** Tiered rows are the persistent (tier 0) and scratch (tier 1) tiers
    31  of con-ron's per-tier tables. -/
    32  declare_arrays checkerArrays
    33    -- byte arrays
    34    | /-- The input buffer. -/ IN : byte := 0

== ConAgua/L/Arrays.lean#L134-L138
   134  /-- **Well-formed**: every number below `tierOff`, the numbers of each kind distinct, only word
   135  arrays tiered. -/
   136  def wf (T : ArrTable) : Bool :=
   137    T.all (fun d => d.id < tierOff && (d.tiered → d.kind == .word)) &&
   138      nodupB (T.ids .byte) && nodupB (T.ids .word)

== ConAgua/L/Arrays.lean#L225-L230
   225  /-- **The surface check**: every array operand of every function of `p` is allowed by `T`
   226  (`useOK`); a function in `exempt` may name any word slot below `T`'s extent (`slotOK`). -/
   227  def ArrTable.progOK (T : ArrTable) (exempt : List FnName) (p : Prog) : Bool :=
   228    p.all fun (f, fd) =>
   229      if exempt.contains f then (Uses.stmt fd.body).all T.slotOK
   230      else (Uses.stmt fd.body).all T.useOK

== ConAgua/Arena/LevelEquiv.lean#L255-L265
   255  /-- con-ron's `lvlEq?` (`Arena/Core.lean:129`) on two level handles: the level algorithm on a
   256  fresh heap (the top reset to `0`). The verdict cache `lvlEqC` is `lvl_eq_c`'s, in front of this
   257  function (`CoreLevels.lean`); this is the uncached computation (`LevelArena.lean`,

   259  -- con-ron: ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:132-149 ConRon.Arena.lvlEq?

   261  def lvlEqL : FunDecl := lfn (u, v) locals (z) {
   262    CTL.u64[192] := 0;
   263    z := call lv_equiv(u, v);
   264    return z
   265  }

== vendor/con-ron/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean#L132-L149
   132  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Level.lean:164-169 isEquiv — `Level.isEquiv`
   133  at two level HANDLES, with the verdict cached on the pair.  `none` is
   134  con-leche's fuel exhaustion and is never cached. -/
   135  def lvlEq? (u v : LIdx) : AM (Option Bool) := do
   136    let s ← get
   137    match s.caches.lvlEqC[(u, v)]? with
   138    | some r => pure (some r)
   139    | none => do
   140      let lu ← readLevelM u
   141      let lv ← readLevelM v
   142      match Level.isEquiv lu lv with
   143      | some r => do
   144        let s ← get
   145        let mp := s.caches.lvlEqC
   146        let s := { s with caches := { s.caches with lvlEqC := ∅ } }
   147        set { s with caches := { s.caches with lvlEqC := mp.insert (u, v) r } }
   148        pure (some r)
   149      | none => pure none

== ConAgua/L/ModelGen.lean#L11-L62
    11  /-!
    12  # Generated word models and specs (`l_model`)
    13  
    14  `l_model` reads the `lfn` text of a group of L functions and generates, for each function `f`,
    15  
    16  * its **word model** `fW : Nat → Mem → Word → … → Option (Word × Mem)` (`Option Word` for a
    17    read-only function, `ro`; no fuel argument for a single function that needs none): the L code
    18    with every local inlined, `abort` as `none`, a load as `rdW`, a store as `Mem.set64`, a call to a
    19    group member as that member's model at fuel `n`, a call to another function as the model its
    20    spec states (`specs`), and the code after an effectful call as a first-order continuation
    21    `fW.k_g` (`| none => none | some (x, m₁) => …`) over the locals it reads, named after the
    22    callee `g` (`fW.k_g_2`, … for its later calls, in source order; after a loop `fW.k_loopᵢ`), so
    23    that a change elsewhere in the code does not rename it. The code after an `if`
    24    whose branches both fall through is a join point `fW.jᵢ` over the locals and the memory (no
    25    copy of it). Equal continuations of the group are shared;
    26  * a function with **several results** (`return (a, b, …)`) gets a list model
    27    `Option (List Word × Mem)` (`return e` is `some ([e], m)`, the end of the body `some ([], m)`;
    28    `↦ fW list` forces it), or with `↦ fW tuple` a tuple model `Option (Word × … × Mem)` (the
    29    longest `return`'s arity, shorter ones padded with `0`);
    30  * a **loop** (`while c { … }` in the `lfn`, or a spliced named block `⟪X⟫` that is one `while`)
    31    is a model of its own, `fW.loopᵢ n m x₁ …` (`exec p n` on the loop: `| 0 => none | n + 1 =>
    32    if c then … fW.loopᵢ n … else exit`; the enclosing code applies it at `n + 1`), over the locals
    33    live at its head. Its result is `(signal, outs…, memory)`: the signal (`Sig.normal`,
    34    `Sig.ret vs`) if the body has a `return`, the locals it assigns that the code after it reads,
    35    the memory unless read-only; the code after it is a continuation of that result. A loop with a
    36    `return` followed by the function's last statement (`return …`, `abort`) is **fused**: its model
    37    returns the function's result. Its spec `fW.loopᵢ.spec` (`⦃s = s₀⦄ exec p n X ⦃…⦄`, by
    38    induction, the model is the loop's meaning) is generated, and a `while` written in the `lfn`
    39    becomes the named block `fW.loopᵢ.stmt` (with `fW.lfn_eq : F = lfn … ⟪fW.loopᵢ.stmt⟫ …`).
    40    Named blocks without a loop are inlined;
    41  * one **guarded equation** `fW.armᵢ` per non-`none` leaf of the `if` tree of each model, loop and
    42    continuation (the path's conditions as hypotheses, in order; on the negative side in their
    43    natural form: `a = b` for `¬ a ≠ b`, `a ≠ b` for `¬ a = b`, `p` for `¬ ¬ p`), each with a `grind_pattern` in the
    44    `grind` attributes; `fW.abortᵢ` for each `none` leaf, `fW.k_g.none` for each continuation (no
    45    patterns);
    46  * the **spec** `⦃s = s₀⦄ invoke p (exec p n) "f" args ⦃LocEq s' s₀ ∧
    47    fW n s₀.mem args = some (r.headD 0, s'.mem); ⊤⦄` of every member (`some (r, s'.mem)` for a list
    48    model, `some (r.headD 0, r.tail.headD 0, …, s'.mem)` for a tuple model), as one conjunction
    49    over the group (`name`), a step theorem per member (`name.stepᵢ`: `vcgen` with the specs of the
    50    callees and loops that member calls, then `finish`) and the induction on the fuel.
    51  
    52  The definitions come in dependency order: each strongly connected component of the reference
    53  graph is one definition or one `mutual` block, well-founded on `(fuel, depth)` if it has a
    54  continuation or a loop (models `(n, D)`, continuations `(n + 1, d)`, loops `(n, d)`; `LevelLeq.lean`
    55  does this by hand), structural on the fuel if it has only models.
    56  
    57  ```
    58  l_model liftGo_spec (p : Prog) (hp : LiftProg p)
    59    fns [(hp.get "lift_go") ↦ liftW, (hp.get "lift_app") ↦ liftAppW]
    60    specs [derB_spec p (hp.get "der_b") n, memoFindG_spec lfSch p _ (hp.get "lf_find") n]
    61    grind [arena_grind] fold [tierW, idxW] finish [tierW, idxW] gen 20 heartbeats 1000000
    62  ```

== ConAgua/Arena/ConsLibRel.lean#L7-L27
     7  /-!
     8  # The cons-table library: the relation and the user API (lane conslib)
     9  
    10  A cons table `C` (`ConsLib.lean`) represents the arena's two `Tbl`s of one constructor (the twin's
    11  `HashMap2`s: persistent and scratch) by **`ConsR C R m on P Q`**: both tiers hold the same nodes
    12  in the same order (node `i` of tier `t` related to `nodes[i]` by the instance's record relation
    13  `R`), the same key → handle map, the node counts at `CTL[ca + t]`, the scratch flag `CTL[1]` is
    14  `on`; and the slots index the nodes (the slot layout, the probing and the growth state, which no
    15  user sees). The L model of every `intern_X` is `consInternM C m ks` (`ConsLibSpec.lean`).
    16  
    17  Both are irreducible outside this file: the lemmas below are the whole interface.
    18  
    19  * **Reading the relation**: `ConsR.flag`, `ConsR.ctl`, `ConsR.cnt`, `ConsR.cap`, `ConsR.rec`,
    20    `ConsR.cons`, `ConsR.back`, `ConsR.recSize`, `ConsR.node`, `ConsR.cons_hit`.
    21  * **Keeping it**: `ConsR.frame` (a writer apart from the table), `ConsR.setFlag` (`CTL[1]`),
    22    `ConsR.reset` (the scratch reset), `consR_init` (the all-zero memory), `ConsR.congr`.
    23  * **An interning**: `consIntern_correct` (it refines the arena's hash-consing, from the
    24    instance's obligations `ConsKeyOK`), `consInternM_frame` (what it writes), `consInternM_word`,
    25    `consInternM_lt`, `consInternM_pw` (the handle word), `consInternM_out` (a hit, or the append
    26    of node `cntC`: the memory outside the slot array is `pushRec`).
    27  

== ConAgua/L/WriteSet.lean#L13-L30
    13  /-!
    14  # Write sets from the program text
    15  
    16  `Preserve.lean` proves once that a program without `st8` keeps the byte arrays and the sizes.
    17  The same induction gives a frame for every function of a *call-closed* set `fs` whose bodies
    18  store only into word arrays of `A` and into words of the control array `ctl` listed in `C`. A
    19  `ctl` index must be a literal `k`, or `k + (e &&& 1)`, which can only be `k` or `k + 1` (the
    20  tier-indexed counts of the stores, `CTL[k + (t & 1)]`). The check `closedW` is a `Bool` function
    21  of the text, so a concrete program's write set is `by decide +kernel`.
    22  
    23  The frame itself is abstract here (`WFrame`): any reflexive relation on memories closed under
    24  the allowed stores. `Arena/Frame.lean` instantiates it with `MemFrame` (the arena's layout:
    25  `CTL` is array 1). Lane `scale`'s spike, made layout-agnostic (DESIGN.md, "The relation's architecture").
    26  
    27  Global variables (`GVar`) are not restricted by `closedW` (a `WFrame` is closed under every global
    28  write). Their write sets are lists of names, `closedG p G fs` (section "Global variables" below):
    29  every run of `f ∈ fs` keeps the globals outside `G` (`GFrame`), and `Triple.gframe` adds that to a
    30  callee's spec for its caller's `vcgen`.

   572  /-- **Non-interference for `L.run`.** -/

   574      (hp : readsIn p S S8 fs = true) {f : FnName} (hf : f ∈ fs) (n : Nat) (vs : List Word)
   575      {m₁ m₂ : Mem} (hm : Agree S S8 m₁ m₂) :
   576      RunAgree S S8 (run p n f vs m₁) (run p n f vs m₂) := by

== ConAgua/L/Agree.lean#L7-L31
     7  /-!
     8  # Non-interference: runs that read only agreeing arrays agree
     9  
    10  `readsIn p S S8 fs` is a `Bool` check of the program text: every function of `fs` that `p`
    11  defines calls only into `fs`, and every array its body names (loaded, stored, measured, copied
    12  from or to, scanned) is a word array of `S` or a byte array of `S8`. The array sets are
    13  predicates (`S S8 : ArrId → Bool`; a list `l` is `l.contains`). A tiered access
    14  `a⟨t⟩` names both tiers, `a` and `a + tierOff`. Global variables are not restricted.
    15  (`Stmt.rdOk` takes the callee set as a predicate too: `readsIn` uses membership in `fs`, the
    16  per-function split for a large program (`Compiler/ReadSetSplit.lean`) a tree of name codes.)
    17  
    18  `Agree S S8 m₁ m₂`: the two memories have the same word arrays in `S`, the same byte arrays in
    19  `S8`, and the same globals. Everything else (other arrays, the number of arrays) may differ.
    20  
    21  **The theorem** (`invoke_agree`): for `f ∈ fs` of a set that passes `readsIn`, two runs of
    22  `invoke p (exec p n) f vs` from states that agree (memories `Agree`, equal locals) end the same
    23  way: the same error, or the same returned values from final states that agree again. `run_agree`
    24  is the same for `L.run`. The proof is the frame proof's induction (fuel, then statements): every
    25  read sees equal data, every write writes equal data to an array of `S`/`S8` (or a global).
    26  
    27  Why: lane parmode (docs/design/parmode.md, Step 4, piece (b2)). A worker runs `check_pending`
    28  in a memory in which only the frozen images and the worker's own arrays have content; every other
    29  array is empty. That memory agrees with the full sequential memory on `S` = frozen ∪ owned, so
    30  the worker's run is the sequential one, which the sequential proof covers.
    31  -/

== ConAgua/Checker/Pipeline.lean#L44-L48

    45  caller's locals and ends in memory satisfying `Post r`. -/
    46  def RelSpec (p : Prog) (f : FnName) (Pre : Mem → Prop) (Post : List Word → Mem → Prop) : Prop :=
    47    ∀ (n : Nat), n ≤ 2 ^ 62 → ∀ (s₀ : St), Pre s₀.mem → ⦃fun s => s = s₀⦄ invoke p (exec p n) f []
    48      ⦃fun r s' => LocEq s' s₀ ∧ Post r s'.mem; ⊤⦄

== ConAgua/Checker/Pipeline.lean#L69-L72
    69  /-- What every stage may assume of the inputs: a 64-bit platform, both buffers below `2^63`
    70  bytes, every word array below `2^64` words. -/
    71  def InputsOK (b pb : ByteArray) (s64 : List Nat) : Prop :=
    72    System.Platform.numBits = 64 ∧ b.size < 2 ^ 63 ∧ pb.size < 2 ^ 63 ∧ ∀ n ∈ s64, n < 2 ^ 64

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L8-L33
     8  /-!
     9  # The compiler from L to Kraken x64
    10  
    11  See DESIGN.md, "The compiler". One pass: an expression is evaluated straight into its target
    12  register by `gen`, with scratch registers; where `gen` does not apply, into `rax` with
    13  intermediate values in fixed per-frame temporary slots (`compileE`).
    14  
    15  **Machine state during L code.**
    16  * `r15` = `T`, the address of the run's descriptor table (`Tab`); pinned.
    17  * `r14` = the fuel counter; decremented at every loop back-edge and every call.
    18  * `rsp` = the current frame; constant while a body runs. Local `x` is the word at `rsp + 8x`,
    19    temporary `t` is at `rsp + 8(nlocals + t)`. The frame has `frameWords` words.
    20  * `rbp` = the trampoline's saved stack pointer; never written by L code.
    21  * `rbx`, `r12`, `r13`: free; the trampoline saves and restores them for its caller.
    22  * `rax` = expression result, `rcx`/`rdx` = scratch, `rsi` = argument pointer at a call.
    23  
    24  **Exits.** `ca_error`, `ca_abort` and `ca_exhausted` are global; they restore the caller's `rsp`
    25  from `rbp` and return to the harness with `rdx` = 2, 2 resp. 1. `ca_abort` is an error whose code
    26  (`Err.code`) is in `rbx` (`abort e`, `if c abort k`: `if c abort k` sets `rbx` before the test
    27  and keeps its one conditional jump; the test itself keeps `rbx`), `ca_error` one with code `0` (a
    28  bounds check, a bare `abort`); both return the code in `rax`. `abort e` may overwrite any
    29  register, a leaf's locals in `rbx` included (nothing after an abort reads a local), but `if c abort
    30  k` writes `rbx` also when it does not abort: it does so only where no local lives in `rbx`
    31  (`Ctx.rbxFree`, `sim_ifAbortK`); in a leaf that keeps a local there it is the general `if`. A
    32  normal return has `rdx` = 0 and the result in `rax`.
    33  -/

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L1550-L1571
  1550  def trampoline (tab : Tab) (entry : FnName) (c np : Nat) : Program :=
  1551    [.label enterL,
  1552     movMR (mb .rdi (tab.save np)) .r15, movMR (mb .rdi (tab.save np + 8)) .rbx,
  1553     movMR (mb .rdi (tab.save np + 16)) .r12, movMR (mb .rdi (tab.save np + 24)) .r13,
  1554     i64 (.push (oR .rbp)), i64 (.push (oR .r14)), i64 (.push (oR .rdi)),
  1555     movRR .rbp .rsp, movRR .r15 .rdi, movRR .r14 .rsi,
  1556     movRM .rsp (mb .r15 Tab.stackTop),
  1557     i64 (.lea (rr .rsi) (mb .r15 tab.args))] ++
  1558    (if np ≤ argRegs.length then loadArgs tab 0 (argRegs.take np) else []) ++ burnFuel ++
  1559    [i64 (.call (.rel (.sub (.label (fnL entry)) .after_current_instruction))),
  1560     jmpL okL,
  1561     .label exhaustedL, movRI .rdx 1, jmpL finishL,
  1562     .label errorL, movRI .rbx 0,
  1563     .label abortL, movRR .rax .rbx, movRI .rdx 2,
  1564     .label finishL, movRR .rsp .rbp,
  1565     i64 (.pop (.reg (rr .r15))),
  1566     movRM .rbx (mb .r15 (tab.save np + 8)), movRM .r12 (mb .r15 (tab.save np + 16)),
  1567     movRM .r13 (mb .r15 (tab.save np + 24)), movRM .r15 (mb .r15 (tab.save np)),
  1568     i64 (.pop (.reg (rr .r14))), i64 (.pop (.reg (rr .rbp))),
  1569     i64 .ret,
  1570     .label okL] ++ loadRes { tab, fn := entry, nl := 0, brk := okL } 0 c (tab.nres - c) ++
  1571    [movRI .rdx 0, jmpL finishL]

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L425
   425  def allocRegs : List Reg64 := [.rdi, .r8, .r9, .r10, .r11, .rsi, .rbx, .r12, .r13]

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L1521-L1533
  1521  def compileFn (tab : Tab) (t sk : NTree) (f : FnName) (fd : FunDecl) : Program :=
  1522    let ctx := fnCtx tab t sk f fd
  1523    let F := fd.nlocals + tempsS ctx.alloc ctx.nr fd.body
  1524    if frameless fd then [.label (fnL f)] ++ fnBody ctx fd ++ [i64 .ret]
  1525    else if ctx.leaf && sk.find (nameCode f) == some F then
  1526    [.label (fnL f), i64 (.sub (.reg (rr .rsp)) (oI (8 * F)))] ++ fnBody ctx fd ++
  1527    [i64 (.add (.reg (rr .rsp)) (oI (8 * F))), i64 .ret]
  1528    else
  1529    [.label (fnL f),
  1530     movRR .rax .rsp, i64 (.sub (.reg (rr .rax)) (oM (mb .r15 Tab.stackLimit))),
  1531     i64 (.cmp (.reg (rr .rax)) (oI (8 * F + 8 + 8 * ctx.need))), jccL .c exhaustedL,
  1532     i64 (.sub (.reg (rr .rsp)) (oI (8 * F)))] ++ fnBody ctx fd ++
  1533    [i64 (.add (.reg (rr .rsp)) (oI (8 * F))), i64 .ret]

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L74-L88
    74  /-- The number of word arrays with both tiers in the table (`a` and `a + tierOff` below `nw`). -/
    75  def Tab.wK (t : Tab) : Nat := min (t.nw - tierOff) tierOff
    76  /-- The position of word array `a`'s descriptor words (lane tiercost): a permutation of
    77  `[0, nw)` that puts tier `1` of a tiered array right after tier `0` (`wpos (a + tierOff) =
    78  wpos a + 1` for `a < wK`), so that a tiered access addresses `[r15 + 8 (t & 1) + d]`. -/
    79  def Tab.wpos (t : Tab) (a : ArrId) : Nat :=
    80    if a < t.wK then 2 * a
    81    else if a < tierOff then a + t.wK
    82    else if a < tierOff + t.wK then 2 * (a - tierOff) + 1
    83    else a
    84  /-- The array whose descriptor words are at position `p` (`wpos`'s inverse). -/
    85  def Tab.wposInv (t : Tab) (p : Nat) : ArrId :=
    86    if p < 2 * t.wK then (if p % 2 = 0 then p / 2 else tierOff + p / 2)
    87    else if p < tierOff + t.wK then p - t.wK
    88    else p

== ConAgua/Compiler/Step.lean#L11-L19
    11  /-!
    12  # One instruction at a time
    13  
    14  The compiler proof is a forward simulation on Kraken's own judgment
    15  `Eventually (step1 Host.exe) Q ⟨d, pc⟩` ("every run from `d` at `pc` reaches `Q`"), for an
    16  arbitrary `Host` program that contains the compiled code. Each lemma here steps over one
    17  instruction form the compiler emits, in continuation-passing style: the hypothesis is the
    18  `Eventually` at the next state, the conclusion the `Eventually` at this one.
    19  -/

== ConAgua/Compiler/Rel.lean#L104-L123
   104  /-- L's memory `m` in the machine's data memory `d`. -/
   105  structure MemRel (G : Layout) (m : Mem) (d : DataMem) : Prop where

   107    nw : m.words.size = G.tab.nw
